mcqs.learning_point: Relate first law to balanced forces
mcqs.question: A book rests on a table without moving. Which statement best explains this situation using Newton's first law?

options.A: The weight of the book is greater than the normal reaction of the table.
options.B: The forces acting on the book are balanced, so there is no net force and it stays at rest.
options.C: The book will move only if a horizontal force is applied.
options.D: The book is in motion but its speed is too small to notice.

mcqs.answer: The forces acting on the book are balanced, so there is no net force and it stays at rest.
mcqs.explanation: According to Newton's first law (law of inertia), an object remains at rest if the resultant external force is zero. In the case of the book, its weight is exactly balanced by the normal force from the table, giving a net force of zero, so it stays at rest. Option A describes magnitude, not balance. Option C is irrelevant because no horizontal force exists. Option D contradicts the observed state.

mcqs.question: A passenger who is not wearing a seat belt moves forward when the car suddenly stops. Which explanation best uses the concept of inertia?

options.A: The passenger's body continues to move forward because it tends to maintain its state of motion.
options.B: The passenger is pushed forward by the seat of the car.
options.C: The brakes create a forward force on the passenger.

mcqs.answer: The passenger's body continues to move forward because it tends to maintain its state of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is the tendency of a body to retain its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. When the car stops, the passenger's body wants to keep moving forward, illustrating inertia. Options B, C, and D introduce forces or actions that are not the primary reason for the forward motion.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly states Newton's first law?

options.A: An object at rest will stay at rest and an object in motion will continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an external force.
options.B: A moving object will eventually stop even if no force acts on it.
options.C: Objects need a continuous force to keep moving at constant speed.
options.D: Only heavy objects resist changes in motion.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest will stay at rest and an object in motion will continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: Option A is the exact wording of Newton's first law (law of inertia). Options B and C contradict the law by implying motion ceases without force. Option D is a misconception that inertia depends on weight alone; it actually depends on mass.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate first law to balanced forces
mcqs.question: If the net external force on an object is zero, what does Newton's first law predict about the object's motion?

options.A: The object will accelerate in the direction of the larger force.
options.B: The object will either remain at rest or move with constant velocity in a straight line.
options.C: The object will start moving in a circular path.
options.D: The object will change its speed but not its direction.

mcqs.answer: The object will either remain at rest or move with constant velocity in a straight line.
mcqs.explanation: When the resultant (net) force is zero, there is no acceleration. Hence, according to the first law, the object maintains its current state: either staying still or moving uniformly in a straight line. Options A, C, and D all imply acceleration, which requires a net force.

mcqs.question: Which scenario demonstrates inertia more clearly?

options.A: A ball rolls on a rough surface and quickly comes to rest.
options.B: A ball rolls on a frictionless surface and continues moving at the same speed.
options.C: A ball is pushed and then immediately stops because of a wall.
options.D: A ball is dropped and accelerates due to gravity.

mcqs.answer: A ball rolls on a frictionless surface and continues moving at the same speed.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is the resistance to change in motion. On a frictionless surface, no external horizontal force acts, so the ball maintains its state of uniform motion, clearly illustrating inertia. Option A involves friction (an external force) causing a change. Option C involves an external force from the wall. Option D involves gravity, an external force causing acceleration.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is a correct expression of Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: A body at rest remains at rest, and a body in motion continues in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an external force.
options.B: A body will move faster if its mass increases.
options.C: A body at rest will start moving on its own after some time.
options.D: A body in motion will stop unless a continuous force is applied.

mcqs.answer: A body at rest remains at rest, and a body in motion continues in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: Option A precisely states Newton's first law (law of inertia). Options B, C, and D are incorrect: mass does not cause acceleration without force, a body does not start moving spontaneously, and motion does not cease without a net external force.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate first law to balanced forces
mcqs.question: When all the forces acting on an object are balanced, what does Newton's first law predict?

options.A: The object will accelerate in the direction of the strongest force.
options.B: The object will either stay at rest or move with constant velocity.
options.D: The object will change its shape.

mcqs.answer: The object will either stay at rest or move with constant velocity.
mcqs.explanation: Balanced forces mean the net external force is zero. According to the first law, with zero net force, there is no acceleration, so the object maintains its current state—either stationary or moving uniformly. Options A, C, and D imply changes that require net forces.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday example that best illustrates the concept of inertia?

options.A: A cup placed on the dashboard slides forward when the car accelerates suddenly.
options.B: A kite rises higher when the wind speed increases.
options.C: A balloon rises because it is lighter than air.

mcqs.answer: A cup placed on the dashboard slides forward when the car accelerates suddenly.
mcqs.explanation: The cup tends to remain at rest while the car moves forward; the relative motion of the cup forward demonstrates inertia. Options B, C, and D involve different principles (lift, buoyancy, magnetism) not related to inertia.
